transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-22
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aria Lopez (Redwood SA); Sara Gomez (Orion Head of ML), Tom Reed (Platform Eng), Priya Nayar (Procurement), Evan Park (Data Privacy)

---
Auto-generated summary: Redwood console walkthrough with emphasis on usage analytics and cost per route. Medium transcription quality; some acronyms mis-transcribed.

00:00 Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh quick intros so I'm Maya, I'll run the walkthrough today, with Liam our SE and Aria on the dashboards side.
00:10 Sara Gomez: Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Sara, head of ML at Orion, said Tom's on for infra questions.
00:15 Tom Reed: yep, hi all.
00:20 Liam Chen: Great. We'll jump into the Redwood Console â€” focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown you'd seen in the deck.
00:30 Maya Patel: The goal is to show how you can correlate token cost to routes and see which end-points drive most spend, so you can tune batching and model choices.
00:42 Aria Lopez: Opening the console now â€” um apologies if the screen share resolution is a bit fuzzy. So this is the main Usage Analytics page, top-left is overall traffic, top-right is cost by model family.
00:55 Sara Gomez: Quick question, are those costs normalized to our committed rates or the hosted list rates?
01:02 Aria Lopez: Good question. Right now the demo view uses list rates; for customers on Dedicated we'll show committed pricing per-account â€” it's a toggle in the billing settings. sometimes the UI label says "list" or "commit" and that can be confusing in older exports.
01:20 Tom Reed: And retention of metrics â€” how long do you keep token-level telemetry? We need 13 months for auditing.
01:28 Liam Chen: We offer configurable retention; default is 90 days but enterprise can opt into 13 months with the audit add-on. We also stream logs to your S3 if you want longer retention.
01:38 Evan Park: And encrypted at rest with customer KMS?
01:40 Liam Chen: Yes â€” logs can be encrypted with your KMS or the Redwood-managed key; we support HSM-backed CMEK in the Private deployment.
01:50 Sara Gomez: Nice. Show us per-route breakdowns.
01:55 Aria Lopez: Sure â€” navigating to Routes. Here each route is a row: route name, average latency, token consumption, cost per 1k requests, and a sparkline for 7-day trend. You can click in to see the token distribution (prompt vs completion) and the model used.
02:12 Aria Lopez: For example, our "checkout-summarize" route is high on completion tokens â€” you can see the cost spike last Thursday.
02:20 Tom Reed: That spike â€” is it user pattern or backend retrying?
02:24 Aria Lopez: The traces pane links to the request sample, it showed a bot-like traffic pattern, we flagged it with anomaly detection. The console also surfaces suggested mitigations â€” like applying rate limits or moving that route to a cheaper model or applying prefix caching.
02:40 Sara Gomez: How does the console recommend model substitutions? Does it run evals?
02:45 Liam Chen: The Optimize module can run workload-level evals and recommend quantization or model variants. For demo purposes, the UI lists a suggested model family with estimated accuracy delta and cost delta â€” these are estimates based on our evals and your prompt set if you upload one.
02:58 Priya Nayar: From procurement perspective we need a clear cost breakdown showing per-route costs for monthly billing.
03:05 Aria Lopez: The Billing export provides per-route CSV tied to token-level usage and model. You can schedule weekly exports to your S3 or BigQuery. We also have a cost-explain view that attributes cost to model+route+region.
03:20 Sara Gomez: Does the per-route dashboard show tail latency percentiles?
03:25 Aria Lopez: Yes â€” p50/p95/p99 are visible, and you can break them down by model and hardware. For Dedicated, we show node-level metrics too.
03:35 Tom Reed: Ok, I'm concerned about mixing test traffic and prod. Do you support tags or environment isolation in the console?
03:40 Maya Patel: Yes â€” routes can be annotated with environment tags. We recommend separate API keys for staging and prod, and the console can filter out staging keys in reporting.
03:53 Sara Gomez: Great. Let's talk tradeoffs â€” we have a strict latency SLO for checkout. We need to know if moving to dedicated will give us predictable p99.
04:05 Liam Chen: Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools â€” predictable throughput. In our experience, p99 variability drops significantly. We can share benchmark runs showing p99 before/after migration. For example, our test on the 8xA100 pool saw p99 drop from ~450ms to ~220ms for short-sequence generation.
04:25 Sara Gomez: That's promising. What about fallback behavior if the dedicated pool is saturated?
04:30 Liam Chen: You can set routing policies: failover to hosted with a lower-cost model, or queue with a latency cap. We can show the routing policy config during a later tech-deep-dive.
04:40 Evan Park: Security â€” we need SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and SOC 2 proof. Is that all supported?
04:48 Maya Patel: Yes â€” SSO with SAML/SCIM provisioning, RBAC at route and org level, and comprehensive audit logs. We'll include our SOC2 report and ISO certs in the security pack.
04:58 Evan Park: And private deployment options? For PII-sensitive workloads we may want on-premises.
05:04 Liam Chen: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem; you can bring your own KMS and we have network isolation patterns. We'll schedule a security deep-dive with our infra-sec team.
05:15 Priya Nayar: Any contract minimums for Dedicated?
05:18 Maya Patel: Typically there is a monthly commit for reserved capacity; we can show a few tiers in the pricing spreadsheet. We'll include short-term pilot options too.
05:28 Sara Gomez: Can we see how cost changes if we change batch settings?
05:32 Aria Lopez: Yup â€” the Optimize tab surfaces batching and KV cache recommendations. There's a simulated savings model: if you enable continuous batching from 1 to 8 concurrent requests you can see estimated cost per 1M tokens drop by ~27% for typical workloads. Note that batching impacts latency for single-request paths.
05:52 Tom Reed: Any nuance about KV cache and session length? Our chat sessions are fairly long (avg 600 tokens).
05:58 Liam Chen: For long sessions KV cache is a big win â€” reusing cached KV reduces compute per token. The console shows cache hit rate per route and recommends cache TTLs. In quantized models, cache behavior can vary â€” we flag that in the recommendation.
06:18 Sara Gomez: Ok this is useful. A couple of minor transcription/labels: sometimes the console shows KV as "K-V" which confuses the auditors, but it's the same thing.
06:28 Maya Patel: Noted, we'll make sure the exported CSV uses full labels.
06:33 Priya Nayar: One more procurement question â€” do you show projected monthly spend under different traffic scenarios? We need that for budgeting.
06:39 Aria Lopez: There's a Cost Forecast feature where you can input traffic assumptions and it projects spend with low/median/high bands. It ties to per-route historical traffic and model choices.
06:50 Sara Gomez: Can we limit exposure by capping spend per route?
06:53 Liam Chen: Yes, there are per-route quotas and org-level alerts. You can set soft alerts at 70% and hard caps to throttle or block.
07:02 Tom Reed: Great. Next steps?
07:05 Maya Patel: Recap â€” we'll send: 1) tailored pricing + Dedicated options, 2) perf benchmarks and a sample telemetry export, 3) per-route dashboard templates, and 4) security pack (SOC2, ISO certs, KMS spec).
07:20 Sara Gomez: We'll review and provide a list of production routes for the pilot and share SSO metadata.
07:27 Priya Nayar: Procurement will evaluate pricing and pilot terms.
07:30 Evan Park: I'll circulate required compliance items.
07:33 Maya Patel: Fantastic â€” we'll aim to get the docs to you by EOD Tuesday and schedule the security deep-dive. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the console recording and the benchmark sheet.
07:45 Liam Chen: Thanks all.
07:48 End of recording.
